review_notes: Independently read canonical and rendered CARDCheck.c lines 68-350, covering every proposed citation and upstream contradiction citation. The sole state_behavior correction agrees with functionality.md; existing names and unchanged inherited knowledge remain supported within the inherited coverage. Acceptance is limited to the change and examined contradiction, not a fresh audit of retained rows.

proposed_facts.reason: Independently inspected all cited canonical lines. Destination selection and peer-copy direction, explicit signed FAT operands, aggregate rejection versus single-copy recovery, destructive reference-map use, chain validation, orphan reclamation, checksum repair, directory-first updater dispatch, and inline interrupt-disabled completion match the proposal and functionality document. Existing names remain appropriate. Accepted deferrals cover downstream persistence and updater lifetime, check-code wraparound chronology, and any specific Melee snapshot call path; none is asserted by this correction.

contradictions.reason: The superseded state explanation obscured the selected slot's role as the copy destination and treated newer-copy chronology too broadly. Canonical code copies the opposite slot over the selected slot and explicitly casts FAT check-code operands to s16. The replacement records these operations literally without asserting wrap-safe chronology.
Single-copy reconstruction belongs to CARDCheckExAsync, not __CARDVerify. The latter rejects every nonzero metadata error count. The replacement correctly distinguishes their behavior.

An in-memory FAT repair does not necessarily dispatch the FAT updater: directory repair returns first. Scratch-buffer mutations also survive early error exits. The replacement preserves both exceptional branches. Whether the directory updater subsequently persists the changed FAT, and its completion/release lifetime, remain explicitly deferred rather than inferred.

unresolved: Downstream updater completion, control-block release, and persistence of simultaneous directory/FAT repairs remain outside the verified change.
Check-code comparison is established literally; wraparound chronology remains unproven.
Generic memory-card infrastructure mapping is retained; a specific Melee snapshot call path remains unestablished.
